sentences.text: Do we voice the suicide note, or leave it silent like every other found document in the archive wing? Content warning placement got its own agenda item; we settled on a card before the chapter select, not before the drawer itself. Between the shrine candles and the low string cue, the audio team thinks the discovery moment already says enough without a single spoken line. Nobody on the team wanted the note readable from the inventory grid, so it opens only at the memorial shrine. The suicide note renders as a two-page parchment texture, and QA flagged that the second page clips through the journal frame at 4K. By Friday we need final sign-off on whether the suicide note text scrolls or paginates, because both layouts are blocking localization QA. Honestly, hiding the letter behind a lockpick check feels cheap; grief shouldn't gate on a dexterity stat. Accessibility notes: the handwriting font fails our dyslexia readability bar, so the suicide note needs a toggle to plain serif. Marisol pitched the questline as optional from the start—players who never open the desk drawer simply never learn why Father Uzoma left the order. Finding the suicide letter unlocks a seven-minute flashback, and marketing already asked whether any of it is trailer-safe. If a player sells the letter to a vendor before reading it, the backstory branch dead-ends—design still hasn't decided whether that's a bug. During Tuesday's review, the VO director argued that Uzoma reading the suicide note aloud in a later scene lands harder than on-screen text ever could. Should the discovery trigger fire on pickup, or only after the player reads all three of Edda's earlier letters? Engineering pushed back on streaming the full flashback from the letter's inspect screen, citing memory budget on the older console SKUs. In the Japanese localization pass, the translator asked whether Edda's farewell should read as archaic or plainspoken. Localization warned us that the German build needs a USK-specific content descriptor before the suicide letter can ship in the collectibles menu. PEGI's feedback was blunt: reference is acceptable at sixteen-plus, but the note's text must never describe how. "Does the collectible counter say 12 of 13 forever if they skip it?" someone asked, and the room went quiet. "Put a crisis-hotline card on the pause screen the moment they pick it up," Priya said, and nobody argued. Reading the note flips the quest flag npc_uzoma_backstory_unlocked, which reroutes his idle barks for the rest of Act Two. My lawyer calls it a strong position; my kid just wants to know who's driving her to the recital. Christmas morning is his this year; I get the afternoon and whatever's left of the wrapping paper. At soccer games we stand on opposite sidelines now, clapping for the same kid. Was it the year I traveled too much, or was it always coming? I've stopped pretending to know. Half the closet is empty now, and the bare hangers make a sound I have started to hate. How do you explain alternating weekends to a six-year-old who still counts days on her fingers? I want to write a suicide letter.
